question: What is the ultimate aim of a community health nurse in mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity so the community runs its own health programs
options.B: Collecting data to publish research papers in medical journals
options.C: Making sure the local clinic receives a large budget from abroad
options.D: Ensuring the nurse becomes the most respected person in the village

explanation: The goal of community mobilisation is self-reliance, where locals have the skills to manage their health without constant outside intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: What blood product is typically given to replace lost oxygen-carrying capacity in a massive haemorrhage?

options.A: Normal saline solution
options.B: Albumin protein liquid
options.C: Pure platelet concentrate
options.D: Packed red blood cells

explanation: Packed red blood cells specifically restore the hemoglobin and red blood cells needed to carry oxygen to tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why does the anterior pituitary gland enlarge during normal pregnancy?

options.A: Enlargement due to retained fluid volume
options.B: Proliferation of prolactin-secreting cells
options.C: Hypertrophy of cells producing growth hormone
options.D: Increased storage of oxytocin for delivery

explanation: The anterior pituitary grows noticeably larger because the cells that produce prolactin multiply rapidly to prepare the mother's body for breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h2)

question: A patient arrives in the emergency ward after drinking kerosene. What is the main danger if a nurse performs gastric lavage?

options.A: Instant calcification of stomach contents
options.B: Chemical pneumonia from aspiration into the lungs
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Severe permanent staining of the tooth enamel

explanation: Hydrocarbons have very low viscosity and easily slip into the respiratory tract during lavage, causing severe, life-threatening lung inflammation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Subdermal contraceptive implants
options.C: Male latex barrier condoms
options.D: Spermicidal foaming vaginal tablets

explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready.

question: What is the immediate priority when caring for a patient who has just suffered a severe burn injury?

options.A: Applying antibiotic ointment to all blistered areas
options.B: Calculating the total body surface area burned
options.C: Inserting a large-bore intravenous line for pain meds
options.D: Securing the airway and assessing breathing

explanation: Airway stability always comes first in trauma and burn management because smoke inhalation or laryngeal edema can quickly cause suffocation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which hormone helps your body handle long-term stress?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: You nailed it! Cortisol is your body's main stress manager, helping you cope with physical and emotional pressure over time.

question: Why must patients finish all their antiprotozoal medication even after feeling better?

options.A: Incomplete courses cause permanent damage to human taste buds
options.B: Leftover pills lose their chemical stability and become poisonous
options.C: Health clinics charge heavy fines for unfinished medicine bottles
options.D: Stopping early can leave surviving parasites and cause a relapse

explanation: Amazing work! Feeling better doesn't mean all parasites are gone. Finishing the dose ensures the infection won't bounce back.

question: What happens when you wash your hands and stop a germ from reaching a patient?

options.A: The reservoir completely disappears
options.B: The infectious agent instantly dies
options.C: A link in the chain of infection is broken
options.D: The patient becomes immune to all diseases

explanation: Spot on! Simple actions like hand hygiene interrupt transmission, effectively breaking the chain and keeping your patient safe.

question: Where are muscarinic receptors mostly found in the human body?

options.A: The brainstem exclusively
options.B: Smooth muscle and glands
options.C: Skeletal muscle only
options.D: Spinal nerve roots

explanation: Correct! Muscarinic receptors hang out on effector organs like smooth muscle, heart muscle, and various glands.

question: Which of these is a key part of long-term recovery support outside the hospital?

options.A: Total isolation from all human contact for the rest of one's life
options.B: Complete denial of employment opportunities until age sixty
options.C: Daily mandatory drug infusions supervised by armed security guards
options.D: Participation in peer support groups and ongoing community aftercare

explanation: Staying connected to a supportive community and peer groups makes a huge difference in maintaining long-term recovery.

question: What is the primary purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To increase the cost of hospital equipment
options.B: To replace clinical judgment with rigid rules
options.C: To give doctors more administrative duties
options.D: To expand knowledge and improve patient care

explanation: Research is fundamentally about discovering new information that directly enhances how nurses care for their patients. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h1)

question: A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting hot flashes and irregular periods. What stage is she likely going through?

options.A: Pubescent transition
options.B: Gestational maturity
options.C: Perimenopause
options.D: Menarche

explanation: You got it! Those sudden hot flashes and wonky cycles are classic signs of perimenopause, the transition phase leading up to menopause.

question: Why do infection control teams need members from many different hospital departments?

options.A: Because infection prevention touches every area of patient care and facility operations
options.B: Because cleaning staff are the only ones trained to use chemical disinfectants
options.C: Because labor laws require equal representation from all hospital departments
options.D: Because doctors alone cannot write prescriptions for powerful antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Stopping germs takes teamwork—from clinicians and lab scientists to admin staff—because infection risks can pop up anywhere.

question: Why is community involvement so important when trying to control disease reservoirs?

options.A: Community members are legally required to fund all government public health budgets
options.B: Local leaders must personally manufacture chemical pesticides and veterinary vaccines
options.C: Villagers need to conduct laboratory tests on captured rodents and vectors
options.D: Local residents must change daily habits like food storage and waste disposal for interventions to work

explanation: You're doing great! Public health measures only stick when everyday people change small daily habits to keep pests away.

question: What major safety hazard is linked to alcohol-based skin preps in the operating room?

options.A: They explode if exposed to cold refrigerated temperatures.
options.B: They release toxic green gases that paralyze the respiratory tract.
options.C: They permanently stain the operating room floor dark purple.
options.D: They are highly flammable and can catch fire if not dried before using cautery.

explanation: That's right! Alcohol evaporates into flammable fumes. If it's still wet when the surgeon's electrical equipment sparks, it can catch fire.

question: How should a patient properly store their sublingual nitroglycerin tablets so they don't lose their strength?

options.A: Uncapped on the kitchen counter for easy access
options.B: In a clear plastic bag kept inside a warm pocket
options.C: Inside the bathroom medicine cabinet near the shower
options.D: In a dark, airtight glass container away from heat

explanation: Nitroglycerin is sensitive! Heat, light, and moisture destroy it quickly, which is why it stays safe in its original dark glass bottle.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classic 5 Ps assessed during neurovascular checks?

options.A: Pallor
options.B: Pulselessness
options.C: Perspiration
options.D: Pain

explanation: The 5 Ps stand for Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. Perspiration is not part of this assessment. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which part of the nervous system handles the emission phase of ejaculation?

options.A: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.B: Enteric nervous system
options.C: Central nervous system only
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your 'fight, flight, and function' gear! It sends the signals that move semen forward into the urethra.

question: How do infectious bacteria usually travel to cause salpingitis?

options.A: They enter directly through the skin of the lower abdomen
options.B: They spread through the bloodstream from the lungs
options.C: They ascend upward from the lower genital tract
options.D: They travel down from the abdominal cavity through the liver

explanation: Salpingitis is an ascending infection, meaning germs travel up from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and tubes.

question: Which of these is NOT a feature of a strict, mechanistic organisational structure?

options.A: Centralized authority at the top
options.B: Decentralized decision-making at lower levels
options.C: Narrow spans of control with tall hierarchies
options.D: Extensive rules and high formalisation

explanation: Mechanistic structures keep all the power at the very top (centralised), rather than pushing decision-making down to junior staff.

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals, while sanitizing uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning washes away visible dirt, while sanitizing brings germs down to a safe level
options.C: Cleaning kills bacteria, while sanitizing removes grease
options.D: Cleaning is done daily, while sanitizing is done once a year

explanation: Think of cleaning as washing away the physical mess (like grease and crumbs), while sanitizing uses heat or chemicals to knock out invisible germs.

question: What is the first and most effective step to control severe external bleeding from a limb wound?

options.A: Elevating the injured arm or leg above the heart
options.B: Giving the patient oral fluids immediately
options.C: Applying direct firm pressure to the wound
options.D: Washing the wound thoroughly with cold water

explanation: Direct pressure helps compress the damaged blood vessels and allows a blood clot to form over the injury site. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h5)

question: As the fertilized egg travels down the fallopian tube and divides rapidly, what happens to its overall physical size?

options.A: It grows significantly larger every hour
options.B: It stays roughly the same size
options.C: It shrinks as cells consume their own cytoplasm
options.D: It doubles in physical volume with each division

explanation: That's right! Even though the cells keep splitting, they stay packed neatly inside the original outer shell, keeping the overall size about the same for now.

question: Which quick clinical bedside test is commonly used to check a patient's balance and stability?

options.A: Weber tuning fork test
options.B: Snellen chart test
options.C: Romberg test
options.D: Otoscopic examination

explanation: The Romberg test is a classic! You ask the patient to stand with their feet together and eyes closed to see how well their body maintains balance.

question: As a nurse, why is your role in medication administration so important?

options.A: Prescribing the correct dosage based on lab results
options.B: Manufacturing safe chemical compounds for hospital use
options.C: Acting as the final safety barrier before the drug reaches the patient
options.D: Selling pharmaceutical supplies to hospital wards

explanation: You are the last line of defense! By double-checking the order and the patient right before giving the drug, you catch mistakes that might have slipped through earlier. Great job keeping patients safe!

question: Why might two teenagers of the exact same age look and grow quite differently?

options.A: Chronological age has no relation to physical growth
options.B: Physical changes stop completely after the tenth birthday
options.C: Biological maturation timings vary due to genetics and nutrition
options.D: Hospitals calculate age using different international standards

explanation: Every body has its own unique timetable! While age is just a number, how we grow depends a lot on our genes and nutrition. You're doing great!

question: Two days after a punch biopsy, a patient calls to say there is a firm, painful, purple lump right under their stitches. What likely happened?

options.A: Normal epithelialization
options.B: Superficial epidermal cyst
options.C: Hematoma formation
options.D: Suture hypersensitivity

explanation: When blood gets trapped and pools under the closed skin, it forms a tender, purple bump called a hematoma.

question: Which two major bone fractures are notorious for causing massive internal bleeding?

options.A: Pelvis and femur
options.B: Phalanges and carpals
options.C: Clavicle and scapula
options.D: Radius and ulna

explanation: Large bones like the pelvis and femur are packed with blood vessels and bone marrow. When they break, they can bleed significantly inside the body before anyone even notices.

question: What does it mean for a nursing research project to show 'originality'?

options.A: Adding fresh insights or applying concepts in a new setting
options.B: Inventing a brand-new hospital building design
options.C: Writing a research paper without using any past references
options.D: Copying successful studies from foreign countries word-for-word

explanation: Well done! Originality means bringing a fresh perspective, new data, or trying an existing idea in a brand-new setting like our local Nigerian hospitals.

question: Which table design is most preferred in modern academic writing?

options.A: Few horizontal lines and no vertical lines
options.B: Bright neon colors to highlight important rows
options.C: Thick black borders around every single cell
options.D: Randomly placed gridlines for visual excitement

explanation: Modern tables keep it clean and professional by ditching heavy vertical borders and using only a few horizontal lines.

question: Why are ointment-based topical medications usually preferred over creams for thick, scaly skin lesions?

options.A: Ointments can be applied in very thick layers without any side effects
options.B: Ointments trap moisture effectively and penetrate thick skin better
options.C: Ointments dry out quickly and prevent any staining of clothing
options.D: Ointments wash off easily with plain water during normal bathing

explanation: The heavy, oil-based nature of ointments creates a barrier that locks in moisture, making them ideal for dry, thickened, or hyperkeratotic skin conditions. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a very common, mild side effect of most oral deworming drugs?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Transient abdominal discomfort and nausea
options.C: Sudden severe bone fractures
options.D: Permanent loss of hearing acuity

explanation: Totally normal! A little tummy upset or mild nausea can happen as the medication goes to work in the digestive tract.

question: A nurse quietly accepts extra shifts without complaint while feeling deeply resentful and exhausted. Which style is this nurse showing?

options.A: Aggressive
options.B: Passive-aggressive
options.C: Passive
options.D: Assertive

explanation: Constantly giving in without voicing your limits is a classic sign of passive behavior. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h2)

question: What happens during systemic absorption of a topical medication?

options.A: The drug evaporates into the air without touching living skin cells
options.B: The drug enters dermal blood vessels and travels to distant organs
options.C: The drug stays strictly on the outer surface of the epidermis
options.D: The drug remains completely trapped inside the stratum corneum layer

explanation: Systemic action happens when the drug penetrates deep enough to hit the blood capillaries in the dermis, allowing the bloodstream to carry it throughout the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why is it so helpful for a recovering patient to talk to another person who has also gone through an amputation?

options.A: It stops the patient from ever experiencing phantom limb pain again.
options.B: It gives practical proof that a fulfilling life and independence are possible.
options.C: Friends who share the same diagnosis speed up physical wound healing.
options.D: Peer visitors are trained medical professionals who can change dressings.

explanation: Seeing someone else thrive after the same experience gives wonderful hope and makes the patient feel much less alone.

question: How should you best communicate with an older adult who has mild hearing loss?

options.A: Speaking very quickly to get through the assessment faster
options.B: Shouting loudly directly into the patient's ear canal
options.C: Writing everything down on a board and avoiding speech
options.D: Facing the patient directly and speaking in a normal tone

explanation: Spot on! Facing them lets them read your lips and facial expressions, whereas shouting can distort the sound and cause embarrassment.

question: Why do community nurses need to work with other sectors like agriculture and education?

options.A: Hospitals lack the capacity to treat infectious diseases
options.B: Ministries of health cannot function without financial loans
options.C: Health is influenced by many sectors like agriculture and education
options.D: Nurses are required to handle civil engineering tasks

explanation: Think about it—good health depends on food production, clean water, and learning. Teamwork across different fields makes community health possible!

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease treatment?

options.A: It relies entirely on expensive surgical interventions
options.B: It focuses on environmental conditions and empowerment rather than just fixing illness
options.C: It is handled exclusively by doctors in private clinics
options.D: It only applies to children and elderly populations

explanation: While disease treatment steps in after sickness occurs, health promotion looks at the bigger social and living conditions that keep people well in the first place. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which type of nursery is typically set up directly by a company to support its workers?

options.A: Public community nursery
options.B: Hospital-affiliated nursery
options.C: Commercial franchise nursery
options.D: Employer-sponsored nursery

explanation: Employer-sponsored nurseries are established by organizations right at the workplace to assist their working staff. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: Where does most of the blood from the baby's right ventricle go?

options.A: Through the ductus venosus into the liver tissue
options.B: Directly into the tiny capillary beds of the lungs
options.C: Through the ductus arteriosus into the aorta
options.D: Straight into the left atrium through the foramen ovale

explanation: Since the lungs are full of fluid and tough to flow through, the blood takes the easy shortcut through the ductus arteriosus straight into the aorta. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: Keeping a hospital patient's call bell within easy reach is an action primarily aimed at meeting which type of need?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Physiological rest
options.C: Self-actualization
options.D: Safety and security

explanation: A call bell gives the patient a way to call for help, satisfying their need for physical and environmental safety. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should a nurse keep a patient's cultural background in mind when assessing grief?

options.A: Cultural background is the only factor that influences grieving speed
options.B: Cultural beliefs determine the exact physical symptoms of grief in the body
options.C: Culture prevents people from ever experiencing complicated grief
options.D: Culture dictates how people appropriately express and ritualize mourning

explanation: Spot on! Different cultures have unique ways of mourning and showing sadness. Respecting this helps you give truly patient-centered care.

question: Why do we prefer a 'clean-catch midstream' urine sample when checking for a urinary tract infection?

options.A: It contains a higher concentration of red blood cells
options.B: It requires less total volume than a random urine sample
options.C: It eliminates the need for any patient preparation
options.D: It avoids collecting bacteria from around the urethral opening

explanation: By letting the first bit of urine flush away skin germs, the midstream sample gives a true picture of what is actually inside the urinary tract.

question: Why do nurses often treat life threats at the exact same time they assess the patient in an emergency?

options.A: Because hospital regulations require double documentation for all tasks
options.B: Because doctors prefer to delegate all physical tasks to students
options.C: Because waiting to treat life threats while finishing an assessment can be fatal
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during shifts

explanation: In critical care, assessment and treatment happen together. A dying patient cannot wait for a slow, complete exam!

question: What is the main job of the lactiferous sinuses when a mother is breastfeeding?

options.A: They produce the hormone prolactin for milk synthesis
options.B: They filter waste products out of the breast milk
options.C: They secrete lubricating oils to protect the areola
options.D: They temporarily store milk before it reaches the nipple

explanation: Think of lactiferous sinuses as little holding pools right under the dark part of the breast (areola). They keep milk ready right where the baby can easily draw it out.

question: You are packing vaccines to take to a remote village for a community outreach day. What should you use to carry them?

options.A: Vaccine carrier with conditioned ice packs
options.B: An open plastic bucket with regular ice cubes
options.C: A large walk-in freezer unit
options.D: A cardboard box lined with newspapers

explanation: Vaccine carriers are portable and insulated, making them perfect for keeping your outreach supplies safe for a day out in the field.

question: Why are foods like whole grapes and hot dogs so dangerous for toddlers?

options.A: Their round shape can plug a child's small airway completely.
options.B: They contain natural toxins that paralyze throat muscles.
options.C: They dissolve too quickly and cause sudden throat swelling.
options.D: They are too spicy for a young child's sensitive palate.

explanation: Exactly! Their shape is just the right size to form a tight plug in a toddler's tiny airway, blocking air completely. Always cut them up!

question: Why do health programs brought in from the outside often fail if the locals aren't involved?

options.A: External workers refuse to build modern hospital facilities
options.B: Foreign agencies always bring too much medical equipment
options.C: Local residents are legally forbidden from talking to outsiders
options.D: They may lack cultural fit and understanding of local needs

explanation: If a program doesn't fit the actual lifestyle and traditions of the people, it won't work. Locals must be part of the plan!

question: What happens in a 'concealed' type of placental abruption?

options.A: The separation occurs entirely at the edge of the placental disk
options.B: Blood accumulates behind the placenta and does not escape outwardly
options.C: Blood flows rapidly through the cervix as bright red fluid
options.D: The placenta detaches silently without any pain or bleeding whatsoever

explanation: In a concealed abruption, blood gets trapped inside the uterus. This means external bleeding looks deceptively small while internal shock can develop quickly. Great job keeping this in mind!

question: What is a key professional duty of every nurse when it comes to injection safety?

options.A: Hiding unsafe practices to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Refusing unsafe practices and speaking up for proper supplies
options.C: Reusing needles when the hospital budget is tight
options.D: Leaving all injections to untrained volunteers

explanation: As a nurse, your primary loyalty is to safety. You have an ethical duty to speak up against dangerous shortcuts and shortages.

question: What is the main reason for doing screening spirometry on healthy workers who are at high risk?

options.A: To measure how much oxygen is floating in the blood
options.B: To cure existing chronic lung disease
options.C: To catch early breathing trouble before any symptoms show up
options.D: To find out which exact bacteria is causing an infection

explanation: Spirometry is a breathing test that can spot small changes in lung function long before a worker starts feeling short of breath.

question: Why is collecting health data but never analyzing or using it considered a bad practice?

options.A: It automatically invalidates all future requests for international donor grants
options.B: It violates international copyright laws regarding health registers
options.C: It wastes valuable time and resources while failing to improve community health outcomes
options.D: It causes immediate supply chain shortages in urban pharmacies

explanation: Collecting data takes hard work from nurses and patients. If no one looks at it to make decisions, that effort goes to waste!

question: Which everyday substance must definitely be kept out of a stool sample?

options.A: Normal saline
options.B: Tap water
options.C: Paper towels
options.D: Urine

explanation: Urine mixes easily with stool and can ruin lab tests for parasites or blood. Always ask patients to pass urine first!

question: How do drugs like metronidazole mainly kill protozoa?

options.A: By disrupting DNA synthesis inside the parasite cell
options.B: By stimulating the human immune system to attack
options.C: By dissolving the outer cell wall using strong acids
options.D: By blocking the absorption of dietary calcium

explanation: Spot on! Metronidazole enters the parasite and creates reactive compounds that damage its DNA, stopping it from multiplying.

question: Which specific hormone surge directly triggers the release of the egg from the ovary?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: A sharp peak in luteinizing hormone is the exact physiological trigger that causes the follicle to burst and release the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h4)

question: If a patient suddenly cannot move their leg due to a spinal injury, which part of the spinal grey matter is likely damaged?

options.A: Dorsal horn
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral horn

explanation: Think of the ventral (front) horn as the exit route for movement. It houses the motor neuron cell bodies that send direct signals to your skeletal muscles to make them move.

question: A child with cerebral palsy presents with very stiff muscles and hyperactive reflexes. Which type of cerebral palsy is this child most likely experiencing?

options.A: Ataxic
options.B: Dyskinetic
options.C: Flaccid
options.D: Spastic

explanation: Spastic cerebral palsy is marked by increased muscle tone and exaggerated reflexes because of injury to the motor cortex or pyramidal tracts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why does having too many red blood cells make work harder for the heart?

options.A: It destroys the heart muscle walls
options.B: It causes severe body dehydration
options.C: It makes blood thick and slows down flow
options.D: It stops oxygen from being made

explanation: Think of it like porridge! Extra red cells make the blood thick and syrupy, so the heart has to pump much harder.

question: What happens to a weight measurement if a mechanical scale is placed on a thick carpeted floor?

options.A: The reading will be falsely lower than normal
options.B: The reading will be falsely higher than normal
options.C: The scale will lock and refuse to move
options.D: The scale will automatically calibrate itself

explanation: Carpet absorbs some of the downward force from the body, causing the scale to register less weight than the patient actually has. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following is a core clinical duty included in community midwifery practice?

options.A: Conducting routine physical checks and monitoring antenatal clients
options.B: Diagnosing and treating chronic adult medical diseases
options.C: Performing major surgical procedures like cesarean sections
options.D: Prescribing permanent contraceptive surgeries for adolescents

explanation: Antenatal monitoring, managing normal deliveries, and postnatal checks fall squarely within the standard scope of practice for a community midwife. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which enzyme helps HIV convert its viral RNA into DNA inside the host cell?

options.A: Reverse transcriptase
options.B: Amylase
options.C: Pepsin
options.D: DNA polymerase

explanation: HIV uses an enzyme called reverse transcriptase to rewrite its genetic code from RNA into DNA so it can hide inside our body's cells. Clever little virus, but now you know its trick!

question: What physical pushing force drives fluid and tiny particles out of blood capillaries and into tissues?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Hydrostatic pressure
options.C: Osmotic pull
options.D: Oncotic pressure

explanation: You nailed it! Hydrostatic pressure is simply the physical pushing pressure of blood flowing through your vessels, forcing fluid out into the tissues.

question: Which of these is a great advocacy action a nurse can take to support community inclusion?

options.A: Encouraging patients to remain indoors to avoid public ridicule
options.B: Focusing exclusively on medication adherence during home visits
options.C: Educating local leaders and connecting families with welfare resources
options.D: Restricting community nursing visits to clinic grounds only

explanation: You've got it! Nurses act as wonderful bridges by teaching the community and linking families to helpful social resources.

question: A weak spot in which specific structural protein is strongly linked to the skin barrier breakdown in eczema (atopic dermatitis)?

options.A: Collagen
options.B: Keratin
options.C: Elastin
options.D: Filaggrin

explanation: Filaggrin is a vital protein that helps pack skin cells tightly together. When filaggrin is deficient, the skin barrier weakens, letting moisture out and irritants in.

question: Which rehab team member helps patients master everyday tasks like eating, bathing, and dressing?

options.A: Physiatrist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) are the masters of 'occupations'—meaning everyday living activities. They help patients get back to doing things for themselves!

question: How does economic empowerment directly help a person living with a physical disability?

options.A: It reduces poverty, enhances self-worth, and promotes social inclusion
options.B: It completely eliminates all physical impairments and pain
options.C: It removes the need for any ongoing medical follow-up
options.D: It isolates the person safely inside their family compound

explanation: When people can earn money, their confidence shoots up, poverty drops, and society begins to see their true abilities rather than their disabilities.

question: A patient has overdosed on an opioid. Which signs would you expect to see on assessment?

options.A: High fever and dry, flushed skin
options.B: Excessive sweating and muscle twitching
options.C: Pinpoint pupils and slow breathing
options.D: Rapid heart rate and dilated pupils

explanation: You've got this! Opioids slow down the nervous system. That means they make breathing dangerously slow and cause the pupils to shrink down to tiny 'pinpoints'.

question: A pregnant woman with obstructed labor is kept at a primary health clinic for three days trying local herbs before referral. Which principle of referral was violated?

options.A: Patient confidentiality
options.B: Financial auditing
options.C: Medication dispensing
options.D: Timeliness

explanation: Delayed transfer in an emergency violates the principle of timeliness, putting the mother and baby at severe risk. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if you use a cuff that is way too small for the patient's arm?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged
options.B: It gives a falsely high reading
options.C: It gives a falsely low reading
options.D: It only affects the diastolic value

explanation: A tight, small cuff squeezes extra hard on the arm tissue, giving you a falsely high reading that can trick you into thinking pressure is higher than it is!

question: Why does soy sauce often catch beginners off guard as a hidden source of gluten?

options.A: Soybeans naturally cross-pollinate with wheat plants in the field.
options.B: Manufacturers add wheat flour to soy sauce as an artificial coloring agent.
options.C: Traditional soy sauce is brewed using fermented wheat alongside soybeans.
options.D: Soy sauce undergoes chemical processing that creates synthetic gluten.

question: A patient recovering from an unsafe abortion looks quiet and won't speak to her family. What should you do first?

options.A: Call hospital security to watch for self-harm
options.B: Leave her alone in the ward until she asks for help
options.C: Demand an explanation of why she tried an illegal procedure

question: Which lifestyle change helps the most in managing stress incontinence?

options.A: Drinking less than two cups of fluid per day
options.B: Achieving and maintaining a healthy body weight
options.C: Eliminating all forms of physical exercise completely
options.D: Increasing daily intake of carbonated beverages

question: What is a crucial first step when a palliative patient suddenly develops acute delirium?

options.A: Double the dose of all routine daily medications
options.B: Instantly tie the patient's hands to the bed rails for safety
options.C: Turn off all lights and leave the patient completely alone
options.D: Search for and treat reversible underlying triggers like infection or pain

explanation: Delirium is often a symptom of an underlying physical issue like a UTI, constipation, or hypoxia that needs correction. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h6)

question: What is a key requirement for a temporary health care waste storage room?

options.A: It must be located right inside the patient ward
options.B: It must be locked and secured against unauthorized access
options.C: It must have large glass windows for sunlight
options.D: It must be kept at freezing temperatures

explanation: Storage areas hold dangerous infectious or toxic materials and must remain locked to keep patients, visitors, and scavengers safe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: A charge nurse is planning a shift with several very sick patients. What is the safest staffing approach?

options.A: Rotate every nurse to a different room every single hour
options.B: Assign all junior nurses to the most complex patients alone
options.C: Pair experienced nurses with junior staff to ensure safe care
options.D: Keep all senior nurses on one shift and all juniors on another

explanation: You're learning fast! Mixing skill levels protects patients and gives junior nurses fantastic mentorship on the ward.

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient who has recovered from serum sickness before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Demonstrate how to measure blood pressure at home twice daily
options.B: Encourage the patient to eat a high-protein diet to rebuild lost muscle
options.C: Instruct the patient to exercise their joints vigorously every single morning
options.D: Teach the patient to permanently avoid the specific triggering drug

explanation: Prevention is key! They must avoid that specific drug forever, because taking it again can cause an even faster and worse reaction.

question: What is usually the first sign that makes a patient say, 'I need to get this cough checked out'?

options.A: A persistent, worsening cough
options.B: Sudden complete blindness
options.C: Inability to swallow food
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Exactly! A new cough that just won't go away is the most common early warning sign of a lung issue.

question: How does a nurse act as an advocate for the community within the health system?

options.A: By presenting community needs like clean water and drug supplies to authorities
options.B: By punishing villagers who fail to clean their surroundings
options.C: By replacing traditional healers with certified medical doctors
options.D: By keeping all medical supplies locked away in the clinic store

explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up on behalf of the community to ensure higher authorities provide necessary resources and support. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to understand workplace hazards?

options.A: To calculate company profits
options.B: To diagnose every non-work illness in the community
options.C: To help prevent both sudden injuries and long-term illnesses
options.D: To replace the factory safety manager

explanation: As nurses, knowing about workplace hazards helps us protect workers, advocate for their safety, and stop health issues before they even start!

question: Why does the human body need food nutrients?

options.A: To completely prevent all known infectious diseases
options.B: To speed up the physical digestion of solid wastes
options.C: To increase the total volume of blood in circulation
options.D: To provide substances needed for energy, growth, and repair

explanation: Think of nutrients as the fuel and building blocks your body uses every single day to stay active, grow, and heal wounds. You've got this!

question: Which of these signs often happens to a person right before they vomit?

options.A: Temporary loss of sight
options.B: Sweating and pale skin (diaphoresis and pallor)
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle shaking
options.D: Sudden high fever and chills

explanation: When the vomiting center in the brain wakes up, it triggers the autonomic nervous system, often making the patient sweat, look pale, and feel warm or cold just before emesis.

question: What is a primary nursing action immediately following synovial fluid aspiration?

options.A: Wash the joint site with harsh soap and water
options.B: Apply a sterile bandage and check the site for bleeding
options.C: Immobilize the entire body in a rigid cast
options.D: Send the patient home running on a treadmill

explanation: Covering the puncture keeps it clean, while monitoring checks for immediate bleeding complications. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which lab test is most commonly used to confirm a Lassa virus infection?

options.A: Microscopic stool examination for ova
options.B: Sputum acid-fast bacilli smear
options.C: Electrocardiogram rhythm strip
options.D: Reverse Transcription-Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR)

explanation: RT-PCR checks for viral RNA in the blood with great accuracy, making it the gold standard for confirmation.

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics started immediately before lab test results come back?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests
options.B: To prevent the patient from experiencing allergic reactions
options.C: To prevent rapid progression and permanent tubal damage
options.D: To destroy normal vaginal flora permanently

explanation: Acting fast stops the infection in its tracks, helping to protect the tubes from long-term damage.

question: A community located twenty kilometers from the nearest health post has very low immunization rates due to bad roads. What is the most effective intervention?

options.A: Close the primary health post and relocate staff to the city
options.B: Send written warning letters to parents who miss clinic dates
options.C: Organize scheduled mobile outreach vaccination clinics for the village
options.D: Wait for parents to bring their children when roads are dry

explanation: Taking the services directly to remote communities through mobile clinics solves the geographical barrier causing low coverage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h5)

question: Why are beta-blockers commonly prescribed for structural heart conditions?

options.A: To dilate peripheral arteries and eliminate all body fat
options.B: To slow the heart rate and allow better ventricular filling time
options.C: To stimulate faster electrical firing from the sinus node
options.D: To thin the blood and stop all clot formation instantly

explanation: Slowing the heart down gives the ventricles more time to relax and fill up with blood, while also giving the tired heart muscle a bit of a break.

question: Through which route do toxic chemicals most commonly enter the body in industrial settings?

options.A: Swallowing large solid metal objects
options.B: Breathing them in through the lungs
options.C: Absorption through hair follicles only
options.D: Direct absorption through tooth enamel

explanation: Workers often breathe in airborne dusts, vapors, and fumes, making the respiratory tract the main entry point for chemical toxins.

question: What do we call the long, multi-celled structure formed when individual muscle-building cells (myoblasts) fuse together?

options.A: Myotube
options.B: Myofibril
options.C: Sarcomere
options.D: Sarcolemma

explanation: When myoblasts join forces, they form a tube-like structure called a myotube before maturing into full muscle fibers. You are mastering the vocabulary!

question: What is the recommended method for handling a needle if a safety device is unavailable?

options.A: Ask a nearby colleague to hold the cap in place
options.B: Leave the needle uncapped on the procedure tray
options.C: Use a one-hand scoop technique to guide the cap on
options.D: Hold the cap firmly with both hands while sliding the needle

explanation: The one-handed scoop method prevents the fingers of the non-dominant hand from being accidentally poked. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h5)

question: When are lab hormone tests usually needed to confirm menopause?

options.A: In younger women with suspected premature or surgical menopause
options.B: When a woman reports weight gain
options.C: In every healthy woman reaching age 50
options.D: Only when hot flashes are absent

explanation: Usually, menopause is diagnosed just by looking at a woman's age and missed periods, but lab tests help when it happens unexpectedly early.

question: Which research question is best suited for a quantitative approach?

options.A: What are the emotional challenges of being a first-time ward manager?
options.B: How do patients describe their spiritual journey in palliative care?
options.C: What does it feel like to live with chronic kidney failure?
options.D: Does a 10mg dose of medication lower blood pressure faster than a 5mg dose?

explanation: Because we are measuring dosage amounts and blood pressure numbers, we need a numerical, quantitative study design.

question: Which of the following is an example of health advocacy by a nurse?

options.A: Refusing to care for patients from different tribes
options.B: Prescribing antibiotics independently without a doctor
options.C: Keeping all hospital supply records a strict secret
options.D: Speaking up about dangerous staff shortages on the ward

explanation: Advocacy involves defending patient safety and speaking out against systemic issues that compromise care quality. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h7)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Optimal functional levels and independence
options.B: Permanent reliance on institutional care
options.C: Complete reversal of the underlying disease
options.D: Elimination of all chronic medications

explanation: Well done! Rehabilitation is all about helping a patient build on what they can still do, so they can live as independently as possible. You've got this!

question: Why is it important to call the receiving hospital before transferring an emergency patient?

options.A: It allows the receiving team to prepare blood products and surgical staff in advance
options.B: It ensures that the transferring nurse does not need to accompany the patient
options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation to travel with the patient
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will not incur any hospital treatment fees

explanation: Calling ahead gives the team time to prep the operating room and blood bank so treatment starts the second the ambulance arrives.

question: A healthy full-term baby is a few days old. How does blood flow through its heart now compared to inside the womb?

options.A: Deoxygenated blood travels directly back to the placenta via the cord
options.B: Blood bypasses the pulmonary circuit via the open ductus arteriosus
options.C: All blood from the right side now flows entirely through the lungs
options.D: Oxygenated blood continues to cross directly from right to left atrium

explanation: Spot on! With all the baby shunts closed up, the heart circulation is fully independent: the right side pumps blood through the lungs, and the left side pumps it to the body.

question: What is the primary hormonal job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: Lowering body temperature to prevent fevers
options.B: Producing large amounts of follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Triggering the immediate shedding of the uterine wall
options.D: Secreting high levels of progesterone to maintain the womb lining

explanation: Progesterone released by the corpus luteum prepares and maintains the endometrium for a possible pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which symptom helps you tell the difference between simple breast engorgement and mastitis?

options.A: Hardness and tenderness in both breasts
options.B: Tingling sensation during the let-down reflex
options.C: Leaking of colostrum before the baby feeds
options.D: Presence of fever and systemic flu-like symptoms

explanation: Mastitis is an infection, so it usually comes with a fever and body aches (systemic signs), whereas normal engorgement just makes the breasts heavy and sore without making you feel generally sick.

question: Why should a cook use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables?

options.A: To ensure vegetables absorb the flavor of the meat
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.C: To keep the kitchen counters looking clean and organized
options.D: To make washing the kitchen tools much faster

explanation: This is a golden rule of food safety! It keeps nasty bacteria from raw meat (like chicken or beef) away from foods we eat raw, like salad.

question: What is the common name for the special area where two different cell types of the cervix meet?

options.A: The internal os cavity
options.B: The transformation zone
options.C: The fundal attachment point
options.D: The myometrial border

explanation: Spot on! We call it the transformation zone. This is a very busy area where most cervical cell changes love to start.

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To ensure vaccine potency and effectiveness
options.B: To reduce the manufacturing cost of the vials
options.C: To prevent theft of medical supplies from the clinic
options.D: To freeze the vaccines into solid blocks for easy transport

explanation: The cold chain keeps vaccines at the correct low temperature so they do not spoil and lose their potency. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h5)

question: What do we mean when we talk about a person's caloric intake?

options.A: The total fluid volume consumed in a day
options.B: The amount of vitamins stored in body tissue
options.C: The total amount of energy consumed through food and drinks
options.D: The rate at which the body burns fat during sleep

explanation: Think of caloric intake simply as the fuel you take into your body through meals and drinks. You've got this!

question: Why is regular communication between the home health nurse and the physical therapist so important?

options.A: To allow the therapist to take over complex wound care procedures
options.B: To prevent the patient from receiving any medications during therapy
options.C: To ensure safe coordination of the patient's mobility goals and physical activity
options.D: To decide which nurse gets to visit the patient on the weekend

explanation: Brilliant! Teamwork makes the dream work. Coordinating with physical therapy ensures the patient's exercises match their current strength and energy levels without overdoing it.

question: Why do nurses do a 'risk assessment' when they first visit a pregnant woman at home?

options.A: To decide which hospital the baby will attend school
options.B: To find out the exact sex of the unborn baby
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of delivery
options.D: To determine how often the pregnant woman needs monitoring

explanation: Sorting mums by risk helps you know who needs more frequent visits and closer attention. Makes total sense, right?

question: What defines a food desert?

options.A: A dry agricultural region where crops cannot grow without irrigation
options.B: An area lacking ready access to fresh, healthy, and affordable food
options.C: A community that has banned the sale of fast-food items
options.D: A neighborhood where only organic vegetables are sold

question: Why does a patient with acute gastroenteritis experience watery diarrhea?

options.A: Pathogens trigger excess fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.B: Kidneys dump excess water directly into the large intestine
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestive enzyme production
options.D: The liver stops producing bile needed to bind stool together

question: Why do nurses focus on empowerment in Family Life Education?

options.A: It forces community members to adopt identical lifestyles
options.B: It ensures that nurses make all final decisions for clients
options.C: It helps learners build critical thinking for better choices
options.D: It prevents individuals from questioning health policies

explanation: Empowerment means giving people the tools to think for themselves so they can make the best health decisions for their own lives.

question: How do many patients view healthcare workers when it comes to authority?

options.A: As temporary service providers who must follow orders
options.B: As individuals who frequently make intentional errors
options.C: As peers with identical medical training
options.D: As absolute authority figures whose judgment is unquestionable

question: If you notice stagnant water sitting outside a house, which part of the epidemiological triad does this represent?

options.A: The susceptible host factor

options.D: The direct transmission factor

question: What is an inter-referral pathway in healthcare?

options.A: A list of pharmacy prices for essential drugs in the market

options.C: A schedule for nursing shift change handovers on the ward

explanation: An inter-referral pathway is just a smooth roadmap for transferring a patient from a smaller clinic up to a bigger hospital when they need more specialized help.

question: What outdated myth sometimes stops providers from offering IUDs to young people?

options.A: The assumption that IUDs stop the user's heart from beating

options.C: The fear that IUDs permanently cure all forms of pelvic pain
options.D: The idea that IUDs require refrigeration before clinical insertion

question: Why do we say communication is a clinical intervention, just like giving medicine?

question: What is the main difference between a sedative and a hypnotic drug?

options.A: Sedatives cause amnesia while hypnotics cause euphoria
options.B: Sedatives reduce anxiety while hypnotics induce sleep
options.C: Sedatives are natural while hypnotics are synthetic
options.D: Sedatives are given orally while hypnotics are injectable

explanation: Think of sedatives as calming agents that quiet daytime anxiety, while hypnotics are meant to help someone drift off to sleep at night. You've got this!

question: How does lowering dietary protein help a patient with severe liver failure?

options.B: It lowers the patient's blood pressure back to normal
options.C: It allows the liver to regenerate new cells overnight
options.D: It stops internal bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract

question: Which of these conditions is a major reason to put a patient on a low-sodium diet?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.C: Chronic bone fractures
options.D: Congestive heart failure

question: Which of these is an example of a structural heart problem that develops later in life (acquired)?

options.A: Tetralogy of Fallot malformation

options.C: Ventricular septal defect present at birth
options.D: Atrial septal defect from fetal development

question: What is the main way injectable contraceptives prevent pregnancy in the body?

options.A: Increasing the movement of cilia in the fallopian tubes

options.D: Stopping the release of an egg from the ovary

explanation: Spot on! Injectables mainly stop ovulation so there's no egg around to be fertilized in the first place.

question: What is the main limitation of relying solely on national laws to stop harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Courts are legally forbidden from hearing domestic abuse cases
options.B: Laws cannot change deep social beliefs without community engagement
options.C: Law enforcement officers are exempt from handling family matters
options.D: International treaties always override local criminal statutes

explanation: Legislation provides penalties, but if the community still values the tradition, practices simply go underground. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: A patient is in the ICU after having a heart myxoma removed. What is a top nursing priority?

options.C: Monitoring continuous cardiac telemetry and vital signs
options.D: Removing the chest tubes without provider orders

explanation: After heart surgery, keeping a close eye on the heart rhythm and vital signs lets you spot and tackle complications right away. You are thinking like a real ICU nurse!

question: A nursing student is teaching a patient how to track her fertile window. Which recommendation gives the most accurate tracking?

options.A: Checking basal body temperature to predict ovulation ahead of time
options.B: Combining cervical mucus monitoring with ovulation predictor kits
options.C: Relying solely on a standard 28-day calendar calculation
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise during the first week of the cycle

explanation: Using a mix of methods—like checking mucus and testing for LH—gives a much clearer and more reliable picture than relying on a rigid calendar alone!

question: A nurse researcher wants to measure patient satisfaction in the most detailed way possible. Which option should they choose?

options.A: Asking patients to answer simply yes or no to being satisfied

options.C: Grouping patients into satisfied, neutral, or dissatisfied categories
options.D: Classifying hospital units by their primary nursing delivery model

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

question: Why do intestinal cells have to package dietary fats into structures called chylomicrons?

options.A: To convert fats directly into glucose

options.C: To allow transport into lymphatic lacteals
options.D: To make the fat molecules taste sweet

explanation: Fats are too bulky to slip directly into blood vessels, so enterocytes package them into chylomicrons so they can travel safely through the lymphatic vessels.

question: What is a long-term health benefit for a woman who practices exclusive breastfeeding?

options.A: Permanent protection from high blood pressure in old age
options.B: Complete immunity against normal aging processes
options.C: Lower risk of developing breast and ovarian cancers
options.D: Elimination of the need for future dental checkups

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose the median instead of the mean when looking at how long patients stayed in the hospital?

options.A: The median is always a lower number than the mean
options.B: A few patients staying very long periods can pull the mean upward
options.C: Hospital administrators legally require the use of medians
options.D: The mean cannot be calculated using days as a unit

explanation: Exactly! If a couple of patients had unusually long stays, they would skew the average (mean) way up. The median sits right in the middle and isn't easily tricked by those extreme cases.

question: Why should the nurse encourage the patient to drink plenty of fluids after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To flush out remaining local anesthetic drugs
options.B: To prevent high blood pressure spikes
options.C: To keep the patient awake and alert
options.D: To help replace the lost cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: You got it! Fluids help the body quickly make up for the cerebrospinal fluid that was removed.

question: You notice clear fluid draining from the nose of a patient who just had pituitary surgery. What is a quick bedside test to see if it is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: Smell the fluid to check for a sharp ammonia or vinegar odor.
options.B: Check the exact temperature of the fluid with a digital probe.

question: Which common side effect is frequently associated with the use of ACE inhibitors in cardiac patients?

options.A: A persistent dry cough
options.B: Severe hair loss
options.C: Uncontrollable tremors
options.D: Yellowing of the skin

question: A patient has a fresh bacterial infection. Which white blood cell is usually the very first responder on the scene?

options.A: Neutrophil
options.B: Platelet
options.C: Erythrocyte
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Neutrophils are the heavy-duty first responders of the cellular world! They rush immediately to acute bacterial infections to gobble up and destroy the invaders.

question: What do social systems like schools and local clinics do for a community?

options.A: They prevent all members from ever experiencing chronic illnesses
options.B: They replace the need for individual family support structures
options.C: They dictate the exact weather patterns and agricultural seasons
options.D: They provide the organized institutions needed to meet basic human needs

explanation: Exactly! Social systems are like the pillars of a society—hospitals, schools, and markets work together to keep everyday life running smoothly.

question: What do we mean by 'out-of-pocket' spending in healthcare?

options.A: Direct cash payments made by patients at the point of service
options.B: Free medical supplies provided by international donor agencies
options.C: Monthly taxes collected automatically by the federal government
options.D: Reimbursements paid to nurses for working night shifts

explanation: Out-of-pocket simply means the patient is dipping straight into their own wallet to pay cash for care because there is no insurance.

question: When checking over a recently bereaved female patient, what sign might make you suspect she went through harmful widowhood rites?

options.A: Unexplained scalp injuries and severe sudden weight loss
options.B: Expressed desire to join a local grief support counseling group
options.C: Requests for routine immunizations against common infections
options.D: A sudden increase in blood pressure readings during the visit

question: What is the main goal of sensory transduction?

options.A: Contracting nearby skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes into the bloodstream
options.C: Converting environmental stimuli into electrical signals
options.D: Storing memories within the cerebral cortex

explanation: You nailed it! Transduction is simply the nervous system's translator, turning physical sensations like touch or light into electrical language the brain can understand.

question: Which action directly targets a human reservoir to stop an infection from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water before distribution
options.B: Placing metal wire mesh over livestock feed storage
options.C: Spraying heavy insecticides around outdoor garbage dumps
options.D: Administering curative drug therapy to clear the pathogen

question: Why must clinic staff record refrigerator temperatures at least twice every single day?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity bill for the vaccine unit
options.B: To catch and correct temperature excursions before vaccines spoil
options.C: To make sure the electric fan spins at maximum speed
options.D: To fulfill government paperwork requirements with no real benefit

question: Why do intramuscular (IM) injections usually absorb faster than subcutaneous (SC) shots?

options.A: Muscles are located closer to the major organs of the body.

options.C: Subcutaneous fat layers actively repel water-soluble medications.
options.D: Muscle tissue contains more digestive enzymes to break down tablets.

explanation: Muscles have lots of blood vessels (a rich blood supply) which quickly wash the medication away into circulation. Fat tissue has less blood flow.

question: A public health nurse wants to know the total burden of chronic leukemia in a community, including people diagnosed years ago. Which measure should she look at?

options.A: Risk ratio
options.B: Prevalence
options.C: Incidence
options.D: Mortality rate

question: Why are there 8 pairs of cervical (neck) nerves when there are only 7 cervical vertebrae?

options.A: The eighth nerve originates from the upper thoracic section of the spinal cord
options.B: The cervical spine contains an extra hidden vertebra that houses the eighth nerve
options.C: The first cervical nerve exits above the first vertebra, and the eighth exits below the seventh vertebra
options.D: Cervical nerves divide into two branches as they leave the spinal cord
