question: What actually happens during the autoimmune destruction of an endocrine gland?

options.A: A genetic mutation stops hormone production entirely
options.B: An infection blocks the blood supply to the organ
options.C: The immune system attacks and destroys glandular cells
options.D: A benign tumor crowds out normal hormone tissue

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! The immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks healthy cells in the gland.

question: Where does a boat (or maritime) nurse primarily work?

options.A: Urban emergency dispatch response centers
options.B: Watercraft ranging from cruise liners to cargo ships
options.C: State-run land-based public health clinics
options.D: Specialized hospital intensive care units

explanation: Spot on! Boat nurses provide care right on the water aboard ships like cruise liners and cargo vessels, rather than working in standard land hospitals.

question: Why do we have a postnatal referral system in place?

options.A: To reduce the total number of patients visiting government hospitals
options.B: To connect primary clinics with facilities that can handle emergencies
options.C: To collect data for national health research and statistics
options.D: To provide routine immunization schedules for newborns

explanation: Think of a referral system as a bridge! It links small community health posts to advanced hospitals so mothers and babies get rapid help when an emergency hits.

question: Why are domestic food refrigerators discouraged for storing vaccines?

options.A: They lack doors that can be locked with a padlock
options.B: They are too small to hold more than two vials
options.C: They consume too much electricity for a clinic budget
options.D: They experience wide and unsafe temperature fluctuations

explanation: Food refrigerators are not built to hold steady temperatures within the narrow range required for vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: What are the two best ways to identify a patient before giving them medication?

options.A: Checking the ID band and asking their name and date of birth
options.B: Looking at the room number and asking the hospital cleaner
options.C: Checking the chart stored outside on the nurses' station desk
options.D: Recognizing their face from walking past their bed yesterday

explanation: Always use two unique identifiers—like checking their wristband and asking them to speak their name and DOB—to keep medication mix-ups away.

question: Which position is best when placing the rectal tip for a barium enema?

options.A: Sims' position (lying on the left side with right knee bent)
options.B: Supine position (flat on the back)
options.C: Prone position (lying flat on the tummy)
options.D: Lithotomy position (stirrups up)

explanation: The Sims' position naturally relaxes the anal sphincter, making the insertion smoother, safer, and much more comfortable for the patient.

question: A patient is admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. What do you do right away?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Standard precautions only
options.D: Airborne precautions

explanation: TB travels easily through tiny air particles. Setting up airborne precautions and grabbing an N95 protects everyone immediately.

question: A patient has a stubborn, hard mass of stool that normal enemas can't shift. What procedure is best here?

options.A: A rectal washout
options.B: An intravenous fluid bolus
options.C: A nasogastric tube insertion
options.D: An oral laxative challenge

explanation: When standard enemas aren't strong enough to break up severe blockages, a rectal washout provides the extra mechanical help needed.

question: Why do older adults get skin tears and pressure sores so easily?

options.A: Increased sweat gland production softens the skin too much
options.B: Rapid regeneration of skin cells creates a fragile top layer
options.C: High collagen production makes the skin stiff and brittle
options.D: Thinning of the epidermis and loss of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Elderly skin loses its natural padding (fat layer) and outer protection, making it delicate like tissue paper. Gentle handling is key!

question: Which hormone helps your body hold onto water when you are dehydrated?

options.A: Thyroid hormone
options.B: Antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Parathyroid hormone

explanation: Spot on! Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) signals the kidneys to save water and keep you from getting too dried out when fluids are low.

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention, like routine screenings?

options.A: Stopping environmental toxins from entering the local community
options.B: Preventing healthy individuals from ever encountering risk factors
options.C: Restoring full physical strength after cancer treatment finishes
options.D: Detecting disease early when it is easiest and most successful to treat

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early through screening so you can tackle them before they grow into a bigger problem.

question: Why are community sources like traditional healers or school registers important in rural disease surveillance?

options.A: Traditional healers are legally required to manage national epidemics
options.B: Rural schools have better medical laboratories than city hospitals
options.C: Many rural residents may never visit a formal hospital when they first fall ill
options.D: Government health workers are forbidden from working outside cities

explanation: In areas with limited healthcare access, community-level informants catch cases that would otherwise go entirely unrecorded. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the biggest safety hazard to watch out for during steam tent therapy?

options.A: Hypertensive crisis
options.B: Sudden hypoglycemia
options.C: Scald burns
options.D: Severe hypothermia

explanation: Correct! Because boiling water and hot steam are involved, burn prevention is always a top priority.

question: Once a fat-soluble hormone gets inside a target cell, what is its main task?

options.A: Activate membrane-bound adenylate cyclase directly
options.B: Release calcium stores from the cell membrane
options.C: Regulate gene expression and protein synthesis
options.D: Block electrical impulses from the nervous system

explanation: Fat-soluble hormones go straight to the control center (the nucleus) to interact with DNA, turning specific genes on or off to make new proteins. You're crushing these physiology concepts!

question: What is the absolute best way to check if a patient is ready to give their own shots at home?

options.A: Ask a family member to take full responsibility for the task
options.B: Provide a written multiple-choice test on injection theory
options.C: Have the patient perform a return demonstration of the steps
options.D: Ask the patient to read the medication package insert aloud

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them show you how they do it lets you coach them, build their confidence, and make sure they are doing it safely.

question: Which of these dairy options is safe for a strict low-fat diet?

options.A: Skim milk and low-fat yogurt
options.B: Heavy whipping cream and butter
options.C: Condensed milk made with whole milk
options.D: Full-fat cheddar and cream cheese

explanation: Skim milk and low-fat yogurt have had most of the heavy butterfat stripped away, making them great choices!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge to health education in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment in every village
options.B: Poverty and economic constraints
options.C: Cultural and traditional beliefs regarding illness
options.D: Language barriers and low literacy rates

explanation: Advanced equipment is definitely not overflowing in rural clinics! Resource shortages are the real hurdle, making this option false.

question: What is the primary natural pacemaker of a healthy human heart?

options.A: Purkinje fibers
options.B: Atrioventricular node
options.C: Bundle of His
options.D: Sinoatrial node

explanation: The sinoatrial node fires impulses faster than any other part of the conduction system, making it the primary pacemaker that sets the normal heart rate. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h1)

question: What should day care staff do when they notice a child showing signs of a developmental delay?

options.A: Scold the child for failing to meet peer standards
options.B: Ignore the sign until the child starts primary school
options.C: Withhold meals until the developmental milestone is met
options.D: Note the observation and refer the family for assessment

explanation: Early identification and referral help ensure children get the professional support they need for developmental delays. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why must strict sterile technique be used when handling parenteral nutrition (IV feeding) lines?

options.A: Sterile technique stops the plastic from melting
options.B: Central lines connect to the digestive tract
options.C: The high nutrient content breeds bacteria fast
options.D: IV solutions contain live active bacteria

explanation: That's correct! Because these IV solutions are packed with sugars and proteins, germs love to grow in them, risking serious infection.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical community resource recommended for families with an infant?

options.A: Lactation consultant services
options.B: Early childhood intervention programs
options.C: Adult vocational retraining centers
options.D: Immunization and vaccination clinics

explanation: Correct! Vocational centers are for adult job training. Families with infants need resources focused on child health, feeding, and early development.

question: You gently pinch an elderly patient's forearm skin and notice it stays tented up for a few seconds before going down. What does this mean?

options.A: Dehydration or reduced skin elasticity
options.B: Excessive fluid retention in the subcutaneous tissue
options.C: Severe local skin inflammation or infection
options.D: Normal physiological response to warm ambient air

explanation: When skin stays up after pinching (poor turgor), it's a classic sign of low fluid levels (dehydration) or normal aging changes.

question: What is the main job of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) when your body needs to hold onto water?

options.A: It blocks the sensation of thirst in the brain
options.B: It increases the excretion of sodium in the urine
options.C: It promotes water reabsorption back into the blood
options.D: It stimulates the adrenal glands to release aldosterone

explanation: Great work! ADH acts like a conservation officer in your kidneys, telling them to save water and make your urine concentrated so you don't dry out.

question: Who typically acts as the central coordinator connecting various specialists and the patient in clinical settings?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The facility security guard
options.C: The pharmaceutical supplier
options.D: The nurse

explanation: Nurses coordinate care pathways, schedule referrals, and bridge communication between patients and the multidisciplinary healthcare team. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for keeping a person awake and alert?

options.A: Basal ganglia
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Reticular activating system
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: Great job! The reticular activating system in the brainstem acts like the brain's alarm clock, controlling wakefulness and your sleep-wake cycle.

question: A clinic nurse counts the total number of pregnant women who received iron tablets today. What is this count called?

options.A: Impacts
options.B: Outputs
options.C: Inputs
options.D: Assumptions

explanation: Outputs are the direct, immediate results of your work today—like the count of services delivered or items given out.

question: A patient doing a 24-hour urine collection tells you they accidentally flushed one sample halfway through the day. What should you do?

options.A: Discard the current collection and restart the entire 24-hour process
options.B: Estimate the missed amount and add extra water to make up the volume
options.C: Extend the collection period by twelve hours to make up for the loss
options.D: Send the incomplete jug to the lab with a note explaining the lost sample

explanation: Ah, frustration! But a 24-hour test has to be complete. Missing even one bathroom trip means the numbers won't be accurate, so it's best to start fresh another day.

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when managing a sudden laryngospasm?

options.A: Calling for immediate medical assistance and emergency help
options.B: Applying 100% oxygen via a face mask or bag-valve-mask
options.C: Administering a large volume of ice-cold water by mouth
options.D: Ensuring the patient's airway remains open and unobstructed

explanation: You nailed it! Never give water by mouth when someone is having an airway spasm or can't swallow properly—that's a major choking hazard.

question: How is spongy bone different from compact bone?

options.A: It lacks a blood supply entirely
options.B: It is made completely of soft cartilage
options.C: It is found only on the outer surface of long bones
options.D: It has a porous, web-like structure instead of solid layers

explanation: Spot on! Spongy bone looks a bit like a honeycomb with little struts (trabeculae), making it lightweight, while compact bone is super solid and dense.

question: Why are injections uniquely risky when it comes to spreading diseases?

options.A: It increases the normal body temperature of the recipient
options.B: It destroys all white blood cells found near the injection site
options.C: It forces medications to travel too quickly through the digestive tract
options.D: It bypasses the skin, creating a direct pathway into the body's tissues

explanation: Our skin is an amazing shield against germs. A needle breaks that shield, making injections a super-highway straight into the body if we aren't careful.

question: What is the main goal of using research in nursing?

options.A: Applying scientific findings to improve bedside patient care
options.B: Writing and publishing new papers in medical journals
options.C: Cutting the cost of hospital drugs and equipment
options.D: Complying with strict hospital administrative rules

explanation: You've got this! Research utilization is simply about taking proven science and using it right at the bedside to give our patients the best care possible.

question: Why do nurses apply universal precautions to every patient, not just those with a known infection?

options.A: Hospital management requires it to save money on lab testing
options.B: Testing blood takes too many days to be useful in an emergency
options.C: Many individuals with infections may be completely unaware or undiagnosed
options.D: Patients get offended if nurses ask about their infection status

explanation: Spot on! Many people carry bloodborne viruses without knowing it, so treating every patient's fluids as potentially infectious keeps everyone safe.

question: What is the main focus of gerontological psychology?

options.A: Pharmacological management of pediatric illnesses
options.B: Anatomical changes of the musculoskeletal system
options.C: Surgical procedures common in geriatric patients
options.D: Mental health and emotional well-being in older adults

explanation: Gerontological psychology looks closely at the emotional, mental, and thinking sides of growing older. You've got this!

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened (but still alive) version of a germ?

options.A: Inactivated vaccine
options.B: Subunit vaccine
options.C: Live attenuated vaccine
options.D: Toxoid vaccine

explanation: Well done! 'Attenuated' just means weakened. It gently trains your immune system without causing severe sickness.

question: What is the main goal of using triage protocols during a mass casualty event?

options.A: To assign patients to private rooms for maximum personal comfort
options.B: To ensure that patients are treated strictly in the order they arrived
options.C: To collect personal financial and insurance data from every victim
options.D: To categorize victims based on clinical urgency and survival probability

explanation: Triage lets responders quickly spot who needs immediate life-saving care versus who can wait safely.

question: Why is the very first cell division in oogenesis uneven or asymmetric?

options.A: Only the smaller cell is capable of surviving outside the ovary
options.B: One daughter cell keeps almost all the cytoplasm while the other becomes a tiny polar body
options.C: The cell divides without copying its DNA properly
options.D: Both daughter cells end up with different numbers of chromosomes

explanation: Think of it as sharing resources wisely. The egg keeps almost all the cytoplasm and nutrients, while the waste genetic material goes into a tiny polar body.

question: What is the main objective of the empowerment approach in health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring that government officials make all health decisions for citizens
options.B: Forcing communities to build modern hospitals using their own unpaid labor
options.C: Helping people gain the confidence and skills to take control of their own health
options.D: Relying solely on foreign pharmaceutical donations

explanation: Empowerment focuses on building self-reliance so communities can advocate for their own needs and solve local health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: Protecting developing germ cells from immune attack
options.B: Providing nutritional support to immature spermatids
options.C: Transporting mature sperm out of the lobules
options.D: Producing and secreting the hormone testosterone

explanation: You're doing great! Leydig cells hang out right between the sperm-producing tubes and are responsible for pumping out testosterone, the key male hormone.

question: If a patient's blood pressure drops suddenly, how does the body try to fix it right away?

options.A: Immediate reduction in breathing rate
options.B: Widespread widening of all blood vessels
options.C: A major decrease in the overall heart rate
options.D: Tightening blood vessels and speeding up the heart

explanation: To protect vital organs when pressure drops, the nervous system acts fast: it squeezes blood vessels (vasoconstriction) and makes the heart beat faster to keep blood moving!

question: Why do many women end up turning to dangerous, clandestine abortion methods?

options.A: A personal preference for traditional herbal treatments over hospitals
options.B: Mandatory government programs requiring family planning compliance
options.C: Restrictive laws, social stigma, and poor access to contraception
options.D: Abundant availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas

explanation: It's all about barriers! When society judges harshly and legal or financial access to safe care is blocked, desperate situations drive people toward risky alternatives. Understanding this helps us practice with empathy, not judgment.

question: Which nitrogenous base always pairs with Adenine in a DNA molecule?

options.A: Uracil
options.B: Thymine
options.C: Guanine
options.D: Cytosine

explanation: Adenine always bonds specifically with thymine to form the rungs of the DNA ladder. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: Your patient has a GI bleed. You notice their heart rate is rising and their blood pressure is falling. What does this most likely mean?

options.A: Normal recovery from bleeding
options.B: Developing hypovolemic shock
options.C: A sudden spike in blood sugar
options.D: Effective fluid volume overload

explanation: Brilliant deduction! When blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to try and compensate, but eventually blood pressure drops as shock sets in. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why is it helpful to have colleagues review your research report before submitting it?

options.A: Colleagues can catch errors and blind spots that the author missed
options.B: It guarantees that the research paper will win academic awards
options.C: It allows someone else to take full credit for the study
options.D: It eliminates the need for any references or citations

explanation: When you stare at your own writing for hours, you miss tiny mistakes. Fresh eyes help spot typos and confusing parts!

question: Which bacterium is most commonly responsible for causing osteomyelitis?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation: Staph aureus is the heavy hitter behind most bone and joint infections. A great microbe to keep top of mind for your exams!

question: Which home feature is NOT necessary to ensure a safe and hygienic delivery space?

options.A: A clean space for the birth
options.B: A large television set for entertainment
options.C: Good lighting in the room
options.D: Access to clean running water

explanation: A television is not needed for clinical safety, whereas water, lighting, and cleanliness are essential. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: What exactly is a 'tropic' hormone?

options.A: A hormone whose primary target is another endocrine gland
options.B: A neurotransmitter that acts locally inside the brain tissue
options.C: A hormone that is released directly in response to blood calcium
options.D: An enzyme produced by the liver to break down circulating fats

explanation: Think of tropic hormones as boss hormones—their job is to travel to other glands and tell them to release their own hormones!

question: Why must the patient's fingers or toes be left uncovered at the end of the application process?

options.A: To allow the nurse to check blood circulation and color
options.B: To let the fingernails grow without obstruction
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling too hot
options.D: To make it easier to paint the fingernails

explanation: Leaving digits exposed is vital for neurovascular checks, allowing healthcare workers to monitor temperature, color, and capillary refill. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is it unsafe to change the needle but keep using the same syringe barrel for another injection?

options.A: New needles never fit securely onto used plastic syringe tips
options.B: The plastic material of the barrel melts when exposed to air twice
options.C: The fluid path and internal parts of the syringe are already contaminated
options.D: The second medication will chemically react and turn into a solid block

explanation: Once a needle touches a patient or medication vial, the inside of the syringe barrel is no longer sterile. Don't risk it!

question: Why is drinking the water used to wash a deceased husband's body extremely dangerous for a widow?

options.A: Waterborne pathogens and infectious diseases from the corpse
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies due to lack of fresh fruits
options.C: Immediate permanent blindness from toxic chemicals
options.D: Chronic respiratory failure caused by cold temperatures

explanation: Swallowing fluids that touched a dead body puts a person at huge risk of picking up harmful germs and infections. Nurse safety first!

question: A nurse manager places experienced intensive care nurses on a quiet postnatal ward while leaving the busy ICU understaffed. Which principle of a good plan was violated?

options.A: Optimal resource utilization and efficiency
options.B: Clarity of financial budgeting
options.C: Flexibility during seasonal changes
options.D: Simplicity of written policies

explanation: Putting the right skills in the wrong unit misuses your human resources and can compromise patient safety.

question: What is spiritual distress in a palliative care setting primarily related to?

options.A: Physical exhaustion caused by lack of sleep
options.B: A lack of proper religious education in childhood
options.C: Disagreements between family members over hospital bills
options.D: Struggles with meaning, purpose, forgiveness, and fear of the unknown

explanation: Spiritual and existential distress focuses on deep questions about life's value, unresolved guilt, and the search for peace near the end of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h4)

question: Why can poor ventilation systems be dangerous in a hospital?

options.A: They trap bioaerosols and allow infectious droplets to accumulate
options.B: They make the hospital rooms too cold for patients to recover
options.C: They increase the chemical purity of the air to dangerous levels
options.D: They cause air pressure to drop so low that patients cannot breathe

explanation: Spot on! Without fresh air moving things out, germs stay trapped indoors, increasing the risk of spreading infections to patients and staff.

question: What is a primary responsibility of a medical social worker in home health care?

options.A: Connecting families with community financial and social resources
options.B: Administering intravenous medications and checking wound sites
options.C: Performing physical therapy evaluations after joint replacement surgery
options.D: Designing exercise programs to improve leg strength and balance

explanation: Medical social workers help patients navigate social, emotional, and financial hurdles by linking them to helpful community assistance programs. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why does high progesterone during pregnancy tend to cause digestive sluggishness?

options.A: It causes immediate dehydration of the gut lining
options.B: It relaxes gastrointestinal smooth muscle
options.C: It speeds up overall bowel motility
options.D: It increases stomach acid production directly

explanation: Progesterone is a smooth muscle relaxant! It slows down the whole digestive tract to give nutrients more time to absorb, which unfortunately brings on that heavy, nauseous feeling.

question: What do we mean by the term 'polypharmacy'?

options.A: Taking only herbal remedies
options.B: The concurrent use of multiple medications
options.C: The total rejection of all prescribed drugs
options.D: An allergy to multiple antibiotics

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking several different drugs at the same time, which happens often when managing multiple chronic illnesses in older age.

question: When cleaning the mother's perineal area before delivery, why must you always wipe from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate uterine contractions and speed up the second stage
options.B: To ensure that the antiseptic solution reaches deep into the cervix
options.C: To prevent the transfer of fecal bacteria into the vagina and urethra
options.D: To make the perineal skin stretch more easily during crowning

explanation: Wiping front-to-back keeps nasty E. coli from the rectal area away from the birth canal, preventing nasty postpartum infections. Simple rule, big impact!

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do when promoting family planning?

options.A: Ensuring client confidentiality during health consultations
options.B: Dispelling common myths regarding modern contraceptive safety
options.C: Providing accurate counseling on various birth control options
options.D: Forcing community members to adopt specific contraceptive devices

explanation: You got it! Family planning must always be a personal choice. Forcing anyone goes against nursing ethics and human rights.

question: What is the primary purpose of essential drugs in a healthcare system?

options.A: To replace all traditional remedies in rural communities
options.B: To provide experimental treatments for rare chronic illnesses
options.C: To generate maximum revenue for local pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To satisfy the priority health care needs of the population

explanation: Essential drugs are specifically chosen because they target the most common and urgent health conditions affecting a community. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: What major environmental problem is caused by poorly operated, low-temperature medical incinerators?

options.A: Complete disappearance of municipal electricity grids
options.B: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the air
options.C: Immediate flooding of nearby hospital wards
options.D: Excessive production of harmless oxygen gas

explanation: Burning medical waste at low temperatures without proper filters releases nasty chemical pollutants like dioxins and furans into our air. High standards matter!

question: Which skin change is a classic sign of long-term chronic venous insufficiency?

options.A: Shiny, hairless skin with thick toenails on the toes
options.B: Painful black sores right on the tips of the heels
options.C: Pale, cool skin that turns white instantly when lifted
options.D: Brownish skin discoloration and irritation around the ankles

explanation: High pressure in the lower leg veins forces tiny red blood cells to leak out into the skin. When they break down, they leave behind a rusty brown stain called hemosiderin.

question: Which condition involves inflammation of the organ that makes lipase for fat digestion?

options.A: Gastritis
options.B: Cystitis
options.C: Pancreatitis
options.D: Appendicitis

explanation: Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas—the vital organ that pumps out lipase and other enzymes to digest fats.

question: What triggers a tapeworm cyst to release its head (scolex) once a human eats contaminated meat?

options.A: Gastric acid and enzymes digesting the cyst wall to release the scolex
options.B: Immune system suppression caused by the larval waste products
options.C: The low temperature inside the human small intestine
options.D: Direct contact with human blood cells in the mucosal lining

explanation: Exactly! Stomach acid and digestive juices break open the cyst, freeing the scolex so it can attach firmly to the small intestine.

question: What is the primary focus of the DASH diet for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while reducing sodium
options.B: Eliminating all carbohydrates completely from daily meals
options.C: Eating only raw meat and root vegetables
options.D: Drinking large amounts of herbal teas and liquid supplements

explanation: The DASH diet emphasizes nutrient-dense whole foods and mineral-rich produce while cutting back on salt and unhealthy fats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h4)

question: An autistic patient gets very upset when you shift their routine by just ten minutes. What core feature does this reaction show?

options.A: An intentional attempt to disrupt the ward
options.B: A sign of sudden memory loss
options.C: A rigid adherence to routines and resistance to change
options.D: A lack of basic physical sensation

explanation: It's completely normal for them to feel unsettled here. Predictability brings comfort, so unexpected changes to routines can cause real anxiety.

question: Which of these is NOT a common mistake when setting objectives?

options.A: Creating vague statements without metrics
options.B: Consulting frontline staff during the drafting phase
options.C: Setting too many objectives at once
options.D: Setting targets in isolation from the team

explanation: Talking to your staff is a fantastic practice, not a mistake! The other choices are classic pitfalls to avoid.

question: What is the primary clinical definition of faecal incontinence?

options.A: Inability to completely empty the bladder
options.B: Painful passage of hard, dry stools
options.C: Involuntary passing of stool or gas
options.D: Frequent passage of loose, watery stools

explanation: Faecal incontinence refers specifically to the loss of voluntary control over the bowel sphincters, leading to accidental stool or gas leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h1)

question: How does a polyvalent nurse usually support the healthcare team?

options.A: Deciding the hospital budget for medical supplies
options.B: Writing hospital policies without consulting staff
options.C: Replacing doctors during surgical operations
options.D: Acting as a communication link between different specialists

explanation: Spot on! They bridge the gaps between various medical professionals, keeping communication flowing for the patient's benefit.

question: Why is spotting a high-risk labour early on so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any postpartum medication
options.B: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient within one hour
options.C: It guarantees the mother will experience a painless delivery
options.D: It prevents small problems from turning into life-threatening emergencies

explanation: Spotting risks early is a superpower in nursing! It gives our team time to step in before a small issue turns into a major crisis.

question: How do benzimidazole drugs mainly attack parasitic worms?

options.A: By blocking cellular glucose uptake and depleting energy
options.B: By stimulating the human immune system to produce antibodies
options.C: By dissolving the outer skin of the host's stomach
options.D: By increasing red blood cell production in the bone marrow

explanation: Exactly! These drugs basically starve the worms by stopping them from absorbing the sugar they need for energy.

question: How many primary lobes make up the glandular tissue of a human breast?

options.A: 2 to 5

explanation: A mature human breast typically contains 15 to 20 glandular lobes arranged radially around the nipple. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h3)

question: What is a common cause of latex allergies among healthcare workers?

options.A: Drinking contaminated water from hospital supply pipes
options.B: Touching metal instruments sterilized in chemical baths
options.C: Repeated skin exposure to natural rubber proteins in gloves
options.D: Inhaling powder from standard surgical face masks

explanation: Wearing rubber gloves all day exposes your skin to natural proteins over and over, which can sensitize your immune system and trigger allergies over time.

question: How does severe kidney disease affect how medications act in the body?

options.A: It immediately destroys the drug inside the stomach.
options.B: It prevents the drug from ever entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It delays drug clearance and causes dangerous accumulation.
options.D: It turns all medications into inactive sugar compounds.

explanation: Since the kidneys act like the body's filter, disease makes it hard for them to clear out drugs. This causes the medicine to pile up to unsafe levels.

question: What does the term 'food security' refer to in nutritional nursing assessments?

options.A: Having reliable access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food
options.B: Eating only foods that have been certified organic by government agencies
options.C: Keeping hospital kitchen supplies locked away from pests
options.D: Storing perishable groceries at the correct refrigerator temperature

explanation: Food security means an individual has physical and economic access to the food they need for an active, healthy life. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h5)

question: A nurse tells a colleague, 'I feel worried about patient safety when medications are left unlabeled.' What communication trick is being used here?

options.A: Avoiding the issue by changing the subject completely
options.B: Using an 'I' statement to express concern constructively
options.C: Accommodating the colleague's poor medication habits
options.D: Using a competing strategy to assert dominance

explanation: Starting with 'I feel' keeps the focus on your observations and patient safety instead of sounding like an attack on your coworker.

question: Besides physical treatment, what else is an essential part of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory reporting of the client to local religious leaders
options.B: Empathetic emotional support and contraceptive counseling
options.C: Permanent hospital admission for psychological observation
options.D: Informing the client's family members about the medical history

explanation: Good nursing looks at the whole person! Along with healing the body, we offer kind emotional support and teach them about family planning for the future.

question: A patient with severe kidney failure is prescribed a magnesium-based laxative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Consult the doctor because magnesium can accumulate dangerously in renal failure
options.B: Switch the medication to a bulk-forming agent without telling the physician
options.C: Advise the patient to take the drug with twice as much table salt
options.D: Administer the medication immediately as ordered without any extra precautions

explanation: Brilliant! Kidneys filter out magnesium; if they aren't working well, the mineral builds up to dangerous levels. Always check with the prescriber.

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

options.A: A simple reaction to eating too much sugar
options.B: Signs of potential pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Normal physiological changes due to increased sleep
options.D: Standard fatigue that requires drinking more coffee

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined in pregnancy are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Grab that BP cuff right away!

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.A: Geographic distance to the nearest healthcare center
options.B: Stockouts of essential commodities at health facilities
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

explanation: Correct! Free home delivery is not a standard reality across Nigeria. Instead, long distances, running out of supplies, and unfriendly attitudes are the real challenges clients face.

question: How does lacking formal education directly impact a girl's future health?

options.A: It guarantees that she will never contract chronic non-communicable diseases.
options.B: It automatically lowers her daily caloric and nutritional requirements.
options.C: It limits her access to health information, financial independence, and safe living conditions.
options.D: It protects her from experiencing workplace stress as an adult.

explanation: Education isn't just about passing exams—it gives women the tools to understand health messages, earn a living, and make wise choices for their families.

question: What are the three core functions of public health?

options.A: Inpatient care, pharmacy, and laboratory
options.B: Planning, budgeting, and marketing
options.C: Assessment, policy development, and assurance
options.D: Diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation

explanation: The recognized framework for public health activities consists of assessment, policy development, and assurance. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: What hormonal change helps the digestive tract get back to normal after childbirth?

options.A: A rapid drop in progesterone levels
options.B: A continuous high output of estrogen
options.C: A gradual increase in resting cortisol
options.D: A sudden surge in human placental lactogen

explanation: Once the placenta is delivered, progesterone levels drop fast, allowing the digestive tract to bounce right back to its normal tone.

question: What do we mean by the 'halo effect' when grading students?

options.A: Using computer software to grade practical nursing procedures
options.B: Failing to evaluate a student due to a lack of time on the ward
options.C: Giving every student a failing grade because of one minor mistake
options.D: Allowing one positive trait of a student to unfairly influence the entire evaluation

explanation: The halo effect happens when a student's polite smile or charm makes an instructor overlook their clinical mistakes. We want objective grading!

question: Why must you give careful discharge advice to a chemical exposure patient who currently looks and feels completely fine?

options.A: Some chemical injuries and pulmonary complications develop hours later
options.B: Most chemical exposures become contagious after twenty-four hours
options.C: Delayed blood tests are legally required to be performed at home
options.D: Hospital policy requires patients to read safety manuals at home

explanation: Some poisons play the long game. Tissue damage can pop up hours after the exposure, so patients need to know what warning signs to watch for at home.

question: For how many months should an infant be exclusively breastfed, according to health guidelines?

options.A: First twelve months
options.B: First nine months
options.C: First three months
options.D: First six months

explanation: Spot on! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives a baby all the water and nourishment they need—no extra water or food required yet!

question: How does Staphylococcus aureus usually contaminate prepared foods like egg salads?

options.A: Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight
options.B: Direct handling by an infected food preparer
options.C: Absorption from contaminated soil during growth
options.D: Cross-contamination from raw root vegetables

explanation: Staph bacteria live naturally on our skin. If a food handler doesn't wash up well, the bacteria can easily transfer straight into the food during prep.

question: What is a very common and dangerous late-stage complication for many degenerative brain disorders?

options.A: Rapid nerve regeneration
options.B: Aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Sudden high blood pressure
options.D: Severe weight gain

explanation: When swallowing muscles get too weak, food and saliva can easily slip into the lungs and cause a serious infection called aspiration pneumonia. You are building life-saving knowledge!

question: A patient started on strong opioid analgesics for cancer pain is most at risk for which common side effect that requires proactive nursing intervention?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Severe constipation
options.C: Chronic diarrhea
options.D: Persistent insomnia

explanation: Opioids significantly slow down bowel motility, meaning almost every patient starting regular opioids needs preventative laxatives prescribed alongside them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h2)

question: Which medication is most commonly given to newborns right after birth to prevent eye infections?

options.A: Erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment
options.B: Hydrocortisone anti-inflammatory cream
options.C: Silver nitrate solution ten percent
options.D: Normal saline irrigation drops

explanation: Great job! Erythromycin ointment is the go-to choice in the delivery room because it safely stops gonococcal infections without causing heavy irritation.

question: Which symptom means a patient might be bleeding too much and needs urgent help?

options.A: Spotting light pink discharge for two weeks
options.B: Passing just one blood clot the size of a coin
options.C: Soaking two heavy pads per hour for two consecutive hours
options.D: Having mild cramping that gets better with rest

explanation: Soaking two big pads every hour for two hours straight is our red-flag sign for heavy bleeding that needs immediate medical review.

question: When the Ebola virus enters the human body, which immune cells does it attack first?

options.A: Red blood cells and platelets
options.B: Epithelial cells of the skin
options.C: Macrophages and monocytes
options.D: Neuron cells in the brain

explanation: Spot on! The virus tricks our body by attacking our own defense cells (macrophages and monocytes) right from the start.

question: Which of these is a classic physical sign that a patient is experiencing acute fear?

options.A: Slow and deep breathing
options.B: Diaphoresis and trembling
options.C: Low blood pressure
options.D: Warm and dry skin

explanation: Correct! A sudden rush of adrenaline makes the body sweat (diaphoresis) and shake when a person is deeply frightened.

question: Which nursing action demonstrates good interpersonal communication during a patient counselling session?

options.A: Telling the patient their cultural beliefs are completely foolish
options.B: Maintaining an open posture and actively listening without judgment
options.C: Interrupting the patient frequently to speed up the consultation
options.D: Looking strictly at the clinic register while the patient speaks

explanation: Empathy and non-judgmental listening make patients feel safe enough to open up and tell you what's really going on. You're developing great clinical bedside manner!

question: How do poverty and transport delays worsen severe maternal illness in local communities?

options.A: They stop the fetus from growing properly inside the amniotic sac
options.B: They directly cause the placenta to detach prematurely from the uterine wall
options.C: They lower the normal blood pressure of the mother below safe levels
options.D: They prevent timely access to skilled medical care during emergencies

explanation: When transport is hard to find or money is tight, simple delays can turn a manageable emergency into a life-threatening situation. This is a huge focus in community health nursing!

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when talking to government policymakers?

options.A: To reduce the time spent in official meetings
options.B: To comply with international nursing trade laws
options.C: To make the message clear and easy to understand
options.D: To hide mistakes made during patient care procedures

explanation: Spot on! Policymakers aren't nurses. Using plain, simple language ensures they actually understand the issue and take action.

question: Who does the WHO injection safety strategy aim to protect?

options.A: Patients, healthcare workers, and the surrounding environment
options.B: Hospital administrators, pharmacists, and medical equipment sellers
options.C: Patient comfort, medication speed, and low treatment costs
options.D: Drug manufacturing companies, shipping agents, and local clinics

explanation: Think of the safety triad: protect the patient, protect yourself (the healthcare worker), and keep the environment safe from hazardous waste.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional pillars of safe motherhood?

options.A: Antenatal care during pregnancy
options.B: Mandatory military service for parents
options.C: Family planning services
options.D: Postnatal care after delivery

explanation: Easy pick! Safe motherhood pillars focus on family planning, antenatal care, clean and safe delivery, and postnatal care—not military service!

question: What is the big advantage of using rapid molecular tests like GeneXpert for TB?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a thorough patient history.
options.B: They provide fast results and detect drug resistance early.
options.C: They can cure the infection without any medications.
options.D: They are completely painless and require no patient samples.

explanation: GeneXpert is fantastic because it gives results in just a few hours and tells us right away if the drugs won't work against that specific strain.

question: Which question is best when a nurse wants to understand how a patient is coping with their sickness?

options.A: Can you tell me your home address and phone number?
options.B: Did you take your prescribed blood pressure pill?
options.C: What is your exact weight in kilograms today?
options.D: How has this sickness affected your daily life?

explanation: Open-ended questions like this give patients room to express their feelings, struggles, and how the illness is impacting them personally.

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.A: To eliminate common morning sickness symptoms during the first trimester
options.B: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn infant
options.C: To prevent transmitting infections from the mother to the developing fetus
options.D: To cure congenital genetic abnormalities present at conception

explanation: Exactly! Catching and treating infections early protects the baby from complications during pregnancy and birth.

question: What is the main drawback of a positive Mantoux (tuberculin skin) test?

options.A: It cannot distinguish between latent and active infection
options.B: It only works in patients who have never received vaccinations
options.C: It is completely unreliable for diagnosing immunocompromised adults
options.D: It requires laboratory analysis of blood within two hours

explanation: A positive skin test simply means your immune system has seen TB before. It cannot tell if the infection is sleeping (latent) or active.

question: In the diathesis-stress model, what does 'diathesis' refer to?

options.A: An underlying vulnerability or predisposition
options.B: The chemical name for antipsychotic drugs
options.C: A sudden environmental crisis or life event
options.D: A physical test used to measure brainwaves

explanation: Diathesis represents the biological or psychological vulnerability a person carries before a major stressor triggers an illness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which type of plan is a charge nurse creating when writing the daily duty roster for the ward shift?

options.A: Tactical plan
options.B: Operational plan
options.C: Strategic plan
options.D: Financial plan

explanation: Operational plans deal with immediate, day-to-day actions like daily shift rosters and direct patient care tasks. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h3)

question: How does the stomach manage to hold a large meal without building up uncomfortable pressure inside?

options.A: By instantly secreting massive amounts of extra mucus
options.B: Through receptive relaxation of its muscular wall
options.C: By opening the pyloric sphincter immediately
options.D: Through rapid absorption of water into the stomach wall

explanation: Your stomach is brilliantly designed! As food enters, the muscles proactively relax to accommodate the meal so you don't feel uncomfortably bloated right away.

question: Which local group is often leveraged in Nigeria to help drive public health campaigns like immunization?

options.A: Traditional rulers and local youth groups
options.B: International shipping companies
options.C: Foreign diplomatic embassies
options.D: Private airline pilots association

explanation: Traditional and community leaders hold immense influence over public opinion and compliance in Nigerian grassroots settings. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h3)

question: What do we call the normal vaginal discharge that a mother passes as her uterus heals after birth?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Colostrum
options.C: Leukorrhea
options.D: Smegma

explanation: Lochia is just the body's natural way of cleaning out the uterus after delivery—shedding old tissue and blood as healing takes place.

question: What is the medical term for an infection in the muscular middle layer of the heart?

options.A: Endocarditis
options.B: Myocarditis
options.C: Pericarditis
options.D: Epicarditis

explanation: You've got this! 'Myo' means muscle, and 'itis' means inflammation. So myocarditis is simply inflammation of the heart muscle. Keep up the great work!

question: Where is the third ventricle located?

options.A: Within the central canal of the lumbar spinal cord
options.B: Directly beneath the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.C: Inside the core tissue of the cerebellum
options.D: Between the left and right halves of the thalamus

explanation: You're doing great! The third ventricle sits right in the middle, snuggled between the left and right sides of the thalamus.

question: A patient comes to the clinic asking about her risk for an ectopic pregnancy. Which factor in her history raises her risk the most?

options.A: Eating a diet low in green leafy vegetables and iron
options.B: A previous ectopic pregnancy in her medical history
options.C: A family history of high blood pressure during labor
options.D: Having a normal, healthy full-term delivery last year

explanation: Having had a past ectopic pregnancy is one of the strongest risk factors for experiencing another one in the future. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h3)

question: What is the primary role of nutrition in clinical nursing care?

options.A: Lowering hospital cleaning costs
options.B: Replacing the need for routine medications
options.C: Accelerating nursing shift handovers
options.D: Serving as a therapeutic tool for healing

explanation: Food and proper nutrition provide the essential building blocks the body needs to repair tissues and fight off disease, making it a key part of medical treatment. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core part of an effective birth preparedness plan?

options.A: Identifying a designated health facility with skilled staff
options.B: Arranging reliable emergency transportation in advance
options.C: Buying expensive decorative clothing for the newborn
options.D: Saving emergency funds for unexpected medical costs

explanation: You got it! Fancy baby clothes are nice, but true emergency readiness focuses on transport, money, and skilled hands to help deliver safely.

question: What is the name of the simple hollow tube that gives rise to the central nervous system in the early embryo?

options.A: Neural tube
options.B: Mesodermal cord
options.C: Ectodermal plate
options.D: Notochord

explanation: The human brain and spinal cord originate from the neural tube during early embryonic development. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why do doctors need specific serological tests in addition to routine liver enzyme tests?

options.A: Routine enzymes cannot detect jaundice, whereas serological tests measure skin pigment
options.B: Liver enzymes show that injury is happening, but serological tests identify the exact viral cause
options.C: Serological tests are the only way to measure how much urine the patient is producing daily
options.D: Blood enzymes only work for Hepatitis A, requiring serological tests for all other diseases

explanation: Spot on! Routine liver tests tell us the liver is angry and inflamed, but serological blood tests act like detectives to tell us *which* specific virus started the fire.
